rounds.text: Yogi Infra Projects Ltd presents a severe profitability crisis, highlighted by a trailing twelve months compounded profit growth of -143% [E15]. This drastic earnings collapse is compounded by negative return metrics, with a return on assets of -0.64% and a return on equity of -0.44%, both vastly underperforming sector benchmarks of 1.44% and 5.76% respectively [E7, E8]. The company's fundamental unprofitability is further underscored by a staggering P/E ratio of -57.42x against a positive sector benchmark of 33.36x [E5]. Compounded profit growth over a 5-year period remains completely stagnant at 0% [E13], demonstrating a long-term inability to generate sustainable earnings. Furthermore, market expectations have detached entirely from operational delivery, with recent price growth exceeding profit growth by 90% [E47], while the company offers a zero dividend yield [E3]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio sits at 0.84x on filed statements and 0.26x against sector benchmarks [E1, E6], alongside strong near-term sales growth signals [E54, E55, E57].

Conceded: trailing twelve months compounded profit growth stands at -143% [E15], 5-year profit growth is stagnant at 0% [E13], return metrics are negative [E7, E8], and the dividend yield is zero [E3]. However, the bear's focus on historical unprofitability ignores a powerful operational turnaround evidenced by surging top-line momentum, specifically sales up 100% year-over-year alongside ongoing quarter-over-quarter and general sales growth signals [E54, E55, E57]. While the P/E ratio is negative at -57.42x [E5], this reflects lagging earnings during a period of aggressive top-line expansion rather than terminal decline, which is further supported by a healthy 3-year compounded profit growth of 22% [E14] closely tracking the sector median of 20.6% [E64]. Furthermore, the extreme asset discount of a 0.26x P/B against the sector benchmark of 6.18x [E6]—and an absolute P/B of 0.84x [E1]—means the market heavily under-appreciates the asset backing while top-line expansion accelerates. Finally, the alleged detachment of price growth exceeding profit growth by 90% [E47] is a natural feature of early-stage re-rating when sales double [E54] off a depressed 52-week base resting at just 27% of its range [E4].
